title: Steering idler arm recall
ask: Has the 1985 steering idler-arm recall (NHTSA 85V108000) been done on your car, or is its idler arm sound today?
why: In 1985 Mazda recalled 1981-83 RX-7s (NHTSA 85V108000): the steering idler arm's pin corrodes once its dust seal fails, can seize, and can break - and then the steering is lost. The fix was a corrosion-resistant pin. Nothing in the record says whether your car had it, and after 40 years the original arm may have been replaced anyway. One 1982 owner who lost steering at 40 mph was told his VIN was not in the recall, so the VIN alone does not settle it. The idler arm sits on the frame rail on the passenger side, holding the far end of the centre link that the steering box pushes. Your answer decides whether the Manual lists it as a known fault to fix, or as checked.
options:
(a) Check it yourself: front wheels on the ground, have someone rock the steering wheel while you watch and hold the idler arm; any knock, visible play, a torn dust boot or a rusted pin means it is due. About 20 minutes, no parts.
(b) Replace the idler arm now without checking: a cheap aftermarket part and about an hour with a pickle fork; a parts round would pick it.
(c) Phone a Mazda dealer with the VIN and ask if 85V108000 was done: free, but records this old are often gone.
(d) It is already done or the arm is new: say when, if you know.
recommend: (a), unless you already know the arm has been replaced - then (d).
stops: Nothing in the projects. It is a safety check on the car as it is driven today; the Manual shows it as an open question until you answer.

title: confirm or check: the words that hide a part
ask: Should a doubt about one detail of a part be written 'check' and leave the part in the Manual, or is every unchecked value 'confirm' and the part hidden until you look?
why: Two words decide what the Manual shows. R11 says a value nobody has measured carries 'confirm' in its note, and the Manual (D-417) holds back any row whose shown cells say it. The research merge (tools/research/merge_research.py) rewrites 'confirm' to 'check' in a part's note when the doubt is about one detail (a bulb's trade number, a wire colour), so the part stays visible and only a doubt about the part itself hides it. That rule lives in a script and its README; no decision rules it, and R11 as written says confirm. It decides how many parts the Manual shows and how many rows Verify asks you about. Since 2026-09-26 a part you have confirmed (parts.checked) is shown whatever its note says, which covers the case after you have looked; this block is about the words before you look.
options:
(a) Two words, written into the rules: 'confirm' hides the part (is it on the car? which part is it?); 'check' marks a detail to verify and leaves the part shown. R11's wording is amended to say so; the merge keeps rewriting.
(b) One word and a column: every doubt is 'confirm' as R11 says, and a new parts.held enum (part|detail) says whether it hides the part; the Manual reads the column, not the prose. Structural, no regex; a migration pass over 974 notes.
(c) One word, as R11 stands: 'confirm' always hides the part, the merge stops rewriting, and the Manual shows fewer parts until each is checked (parts.checked).
recommend: (a), unless you would rather the rule be a column than a word - then (b).
stops: Which words the research merge writes (tools/research, waves 2 and 3), and how many parts the Manual shows before you have looked at them.
